status_summary: On 2025-09-19 HHS announced a safety review of the mifepristone REMS (the 2023 REMS allows telehealth prescribing and mail or retail pharmacy dispensing), and on 2025-09-30 FDA approved an additional generic mifepristone under the same REMS. As of 2026-10-07 no completed review, REMS change or label change was found, and FDA's page documenting the REMS was last updated 2025-01-17. In an April 2026 filing the Justice Department described the review as including a new study and as expected to take under a year from September 2025 (per the Center for Reproductive Rights), and a Louisiana district court set 2026-10-07 for a status report, whose content was not found. Courts have deferred to the review: the Western District of Louisiana paused Louisiana v. FDA for six months in April 2026, and a Texas federal court paused Texas and Florida's suit against the 2000 approval until 2026-12-01 or completion of the review (reported 2026-09-01). A Fifth Circuit order of 2026-05-01 reinstating in-person dispensing nationwide was blocked by the Supreme Court on 2026-05-14 (two justices dissenting); the Fifth Circuit heard argument on Louisiana's appeal on 2026-09-09 (No. 26-30203) and no ruling was found. The FDA Commissioner left in May 2026; the nominee, Heidi Overton, told the Senate HELP Committee on 2026-09-24 that FDA has found the drug safe and effective with its risk mitigation requirements, declined to predict the review's outcome, and awaited a committee vote.

timeline.event: HHS Secretary announces a review of the mifepristone REMS, launched through a September 2025 letter from the Secretary and the FDA Commissioner to Republican state attorneys general.

FDA approves an additional generic mifepristone under the same REMS (a second generic sponsor; the approval is not a withdrawal or tightening, and runs against the Mandate's call to stop approving mail-order distribution).

Louisiana sues FDA over the 2023 REMS (October 2025; exact day not given, first of month used). In the same month a federal court in Hawaii (Purcell v. Kennedy; the order is labeled 2025-10-30 in a link KFF cites) finds FDA did not give a reasoned explanation for keeping certain restrictions in 2023 and orders review of overlooked evidence.

In Louisiana v. FDA, which the Western District of Louisiana had paused for six months earlier in April so FDA could continue its review, the Justice Department files a brief describing a REMS review that includes a new study and is expected to take under a year from September 2025; a status report on the review is due 2026-10-07 (per the Center for Reproductive Rights; the brief itself was not read).

The Supreme Court blocks the Fifth Circuit's 2026-05-01 order (which had reinstated in-person dispensing nationwide pending appeal), Justices Alito and Thomas dissenting; the 2023 REMS stays in effect while the case returns to the Fifth Circuit.

A report dated 2026-09-01 says the Northern District of Texas (Judge Reed O'Connor) paused the Texas and Florida suit seeking to revoke the 2000 mifepristone approval, at the Justice Department's request and with the states' agreement, until 2026-12-01 or completion of FDA's safety review, whichever comes first; the report says an administration official stated in June that the review would likely take about six months.

A three-judge Fifth Circuit panel hears argument in Louisiana v. FDA (No. 26-30203) on Louisiana's request to stay the 2023 REMS changes; the panel raised whether it can reimpose a stay the Supreme Court blocked and whether Louisiana has standing, and gave no ruling date. A Justice Department lawyer argued Louisiana lacks standing.

At her Senate HELP Committee confirmation hearing as FDA Commissioner nominee (the prior Commissioner left in May), Heidi Overton says FDA has found mifepristone safe and effective with its risk mitigation requirements, would not say whether she agrees or predict the outcome of FDA's internal review, and the committee has not yet voted.

title: Restore in-person dispensing and stricter FDA rules for mifepristone, or withdraw approval
uncertainties: No FDA or HHS primary document announcing the review or the generic approval could be reached (the FDA mifepristone page was last updated 2025-01-17); the September 2025 dates come from KFF, and an earlier review noted a Wikipedia entry placing the generic approval in October 2025 (citing Politico and PBS), a few days later than KFF's 2025-09-30. A Federal Register query for 'mifepristone' since 2025-01-20 returned only a VA rule, an HHS pharmacy-guidance rescission and an NIH patent-license notice, no FDA REMS action. The outcome of the 2026-10-07 status report was not found (the date is today). The April 2026 DOJ brief is described through a Center for Reproductive Rights summary (an advocacy source) and was not read; the Texas and Florida pause comes from a syndicated report whose order date is inferred as the Sunday before its 2026-09-01 date; the Fifth Circuit argument is from Bloomberg Law and the nominee's remarks from Fierce Pharma, both read through summarizing fetches. The Fifth Circuit has not ruled in any source found. Source dates for the CRR, NewsChannel 9, Bloomberg Law and Fierce items are the filing, report or event dates, not confirmed publication dates. The Mandate text on p. 458 says to restore the REMS by removing the in-person requirement, which appears to be a drafting slip; I read it as restoring in-person dispensing, consistent with p. 459. Month-only events use the first of the month. Stage proposed (12) rests on a review that is announced and underway but has produced no operative change; match is changed from direct to partial because the review is not itself a step that tracks the specific restrictions the Mandate lists.
